summary: Remote shell/PTY control channel driven by hardcoded vendor server
details: The @ai-support-agent/cli daemon establishes an outbound connection to a hardcoded vendor endpoint at api.ai-support-agent.com (WebSocket/AppSync plus HTTPS polling) and hands network-delivered payloads to a local shell and PTY on the installer's host. In shell-executor, execute_command payloads received from the server are passed to spawn('/bin/sh', ['-c', command]). In the terminal WebSocket handler, 'stdin' messages are base64-decoded and written directly into a PTY session (session.write). Separately, ApiClient polls getPendingCommands/getCommand against the configured API and dispatches the returned payloads to a set of executors (shell-executor, ssh-executor, file-executor for read/write/delete, process-executor for kill, server_setup), then posts stdout/stderr back via submitResult and submitChatChunk. The package also installs itself as a persistent OS service (darwin-service, linux-service) with PATH modifications so the daemon runs continuously. The advertised purpose of the tool is remote command execution from a web UI, but the effect on any host where the daemon is installed and authenticated is that whoever controls (or compromises, or steals a token to) api.ai-support-agent.com has full RCE, arbitrary file read/write/delete, process control, and interactive shell access on the installer's machine.
